rows.description: A parent or roommate sees someone gasping and terrified and feels scared too. Staying steady and kind, without panic, gives the person an anchor, and follow-up care matters.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17

rows.subtype: Rituals to keep bad things away [Actor]
rows.description: A child repeats handwashing, touching or checking, or must say certain words to prevent harm. It feels unavoidable, and scolding makes it worse; a doctor or child psychologist can guide the family.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A family may repeat answers, wait outside or change routines to keep the person calm. It comes from love but can strengthen the pattern, and a clinician can advise how to help without feeding it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager may have upsetting thoughts they hate and fear meaning something about them. Such thoughts are common and do not show who a person is; shame keeps them secret, and professional help works.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult spends hours checking or arranging things, arrives late and hides it from friends. Compulsions relieve fear briefly and then demand more, and seeking a qualified clinician is wise.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child startles at loud sounds, has nightmares or plays out scary scenes again and again, or shuts down when reminded. Safety, routine and trusted adults help, and a child specialist is worth seeing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: After frightening events, a teenager may go numb, become jumpy, lash out, run away or please everyone to stay safe. These are protective survival responses, not character faults.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22
related mind states: fear, detachment, trust

rows.description: A teacher sees a student who explodes or goes silent over small things. Asking what happened rather than what is wrong, predictable routines and no public shaming help, with referral to a counsellor.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22

rows.subtype: Feeling unsafe in a safe place [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult may feel on edge, avoid reminders, feel detached or ashamed and struggle to trust. Healing usually needs time, safety and support from someone trained, not just willpower.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: shame, detachment, trust

rows.description: A person supporting a survivor may feel confused when the survivor pulls away or reacts strongly. Patience, asking what helps and respecting pace, without pushing for details, create safety.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: admiration, confusion, trust
